answer: Agents can limit Sybil influence by requiring each account to lock a scarce, slashable stake before it votes on a task, then weighting votes by stake and randomly auditing results. A kernel of independent reviewers can challenge a suspicious cluster; if an audit finds coordinated fraud, the protocol burns the offenders’ deposits and rewards the challengers. The yarrow-style random audits make evasion uncertain, while the pulse of ongoing tasks forces attackers to keep capital locked and risk repeated losses.
